metadata.chapter_subtitle: Trilateration, clock bias, and the geometry of space-based positioning

inventory.summary: The GPS chapter was already strong, but it benefited from clearer opening guidance so trilateration, pseudorange, and clock bias were framed before the nonlinear system appears.
issues: The chapter needed a learner-facing setup block despite its strong technical content.
Clock bias is the main conceptual surprise and deserved to be highlighted earlier.
The orbital mechanics cluster in topic libraries reads more consistently when the same onboarding pattern is used.

rewrite.summary: Added a clearer chapter ramp and preserved the trilateration and least-squares derivation.
editor_notes: Added a Before You Start section.
Used the opening to foreground distance spheres and receiver clock bias.
Left the technical solution structure intact because it already fits the volume.

qa_review.summary: The chapter now introduces the GPS positioning problem more gently while preserving the mathematical accuracy of the nonlinear pseudorange model.

repair.summary: The chapter was repaired by adding better onboarding rather than by changing the core mathematics.
actions_taken: Added a Before You Start section.
Brought the trilateration picture forward in the reader's path.
Kept the iterative least-squares treatment unchanged.

design_review.summary: The chapter already leverages visuals and interactivity strongly, and the revised introduction makes those tools easier to read.
improvements_made: Added reader-facing prerequisite and focus guidance.
Preserved the chapter's rich interactive and geometric explainer treatment.
Improved interpretive support around the role of the fourth satellite.
